summary: Correct for the specified source-level dependency-queue contract; no concrete blocking or nonblocking defect found in the two new artifacts.

checks.name: Manifest and source syntax
checks.result: All 12 byte counts and SHA-256 values match the sealed manifest; all seven Python inputs parse with stdlib AST. Manifest digest matches the initial observation.

checks.name: Exact first-check gate and terminal-only polling
checks.result: The launcher passes 2026-10-15T23:39:58.342327+00:00, exactly the same instant as 2026-10-16T07:39:58.342327+08:00. The queue saves only its own initial state and sleeps until this deadline before inspecting pair_exit.json. Missing exits and occupied authorized cards cause a 300-second sleep. No parent progress/log reads occur; parent completion and GPU memory are inspected only after an actual successful parent exit.

checks.name: Parent terminal receipt producer/consumer contract
checks.result: The executed parent wrapper uses subprocess.run and writes actual_controller_exit_code from its returned process status. Its embedded driver AST equals the separate parent_driver.py. The driver waits for both children, requires actual exit codes [0,0], validates all 20 matched clip orders, and checks both full-training/three-benchmark receipts, full98_selection_complete, and exact lasher/rgbt234/rgbt210 report keys before writing pair_complete.json. The queue consumes these exact names/status values. A nonzero parent exit returns failure before any GPU query or controller launch.

checks.name: Authorized-card release and one controller launch
checks.result: The only queue GPU query is nvidia-smi -i 2,3 for index,memory.used,memory.total; both indexes must match and both memory values must be below 500 MiB. Occupied cards wait. The single Popen site is after the dependency/capacity loop and has no retry path. It starts the CPU orchestration process with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES empty. The downstream controller rechecks cards and restricts its run helper devices to 2,3 or CPU. No GPU0/1/27 use, preemption, temperature/power operation, package operation, or deletion is introduced.

checks.name: Frozen command, source scope, paths and interpreter
checks.result: The launcher requires the existing /data/wangwj/envs/CADTrack/bin/python and ssh2028 warm-existing-environment declaration. The queue requires its current interpreter and cadtrack_abc.dense_main_pipeline, verifies the same parent root, and launches the scope command unchanged. Every required controller flag is supplied, no unknown/duplicate flag occurs, and batch128 is accepted. Config, query, baseline and output paths are absolute and consistent. Queue output and main output are distinct. Existing queue/controller digests match the sealed bytes. Existing scope source checks are reused at startup and before controller launch; no new hash scheme is proposed.

checks.name: Generated wrapper and actual subprocess exit semantics
checks.result: Only the wrapper-text expression was evaluated in memory using fixed PurePosixPath values and the explicit command; generated Python parses and contains real newline characters. It runs the dependency queue synchronously and writes queue_exit.json actual_queue_exit_code from result.returncode. The queue records child.wait() as actual_main_controller_exit_code and reports a failed main controller for a nonzero code. The wrapper itself can exit normally after recording a failed queue; success must be read from the actual_queue_exit_code receipt, not inferred from the wrapper OS exit. No reviewed consumer confuses these meanings.

checks.name: Startup verification is restricted to the new CPU queue and wrapper
checks.result: The verification block reads only the new queue_state.json and /proc cmdlines for its queue_pid and the newly created wrapper PID. Both byte replacements use an actual NUL separator. It requires WAITING_UNTIL_NOT_BEFORE, null last_dependency_check_utc, launch_count0 and main_controller_started false. The launcher has no GPU-query subprocess, parent log/progress read, or existing observer/handle probe. Source/config reads and disk_usage are startup preparation, not current parent/GPU observations. The package initializer is docstring-only and the two new artifacts import stdlib only.

checks.name: Downstream orchestration ownership and completion fields
checks.result: The frozen main controller owns native qualification, raw/control probes, matched full20 continuations, full98 selection and all three formal reports, fresh evidence/calibration, fresh consequences/policy fitting, and main full98/formal reports. Its completion receipt produces DENSE_R3_COMPLETE_TRAINING_AND_EVALUATION, full_ABC_training_complete and seven_metric_plus_two exactly as the queue consumes them. Source flow and field compatibility are checked here; the underlying scientific modules are not re-reviewed or executed.

checks.name: No training or effectiveness claims from a waiting queue
checks.result: Initial records explicitly say CPU_DEPENDENCY_QUEUE_LAUNCHED, neural_jobs_started0 and new_main_pipeline_started false. Later state distinguishes a main-controller Popen from NN training/evaluation evidence. Even successful pipeline completion leaves goal_achieved false, preserves seven_metric_plus_two, and retains the requirement for matched ablations and result audit before claiming component effectiveness. The frozen scope explicitly says R3 GPU qualification and full ABC training have not occurred.

checks.name: Five supplied host tests are honestly described
checks.result: The five test methods and recorded PASS cases match: before_deadline, parent_failed, busy_then_free, child_failed and success. They patch sleep/time and subprocess.run/Popen; fixtures are explicitly synthetic and metrics null. Their assertions cover zero pre-deadline launch/capacity calls, parent-failure stop, busy-to-free 300-second wait, one CPU-controller launch, child-failure propagation, and completion without goal success. Reviewer did not re-run this script because it is hardcoded to production source locations; this review instead inspected its AST/source and supplied result. These tests do not prove real subprocess/GPU/remote operation or experimental results.

limitations: Source-only review of the two new artifacts, bounded to the manifest and its 12 sealed inputs. Original paths, SSH/server state, current GPU/training state, other processes/agents, and existing observer handles were not inspected.

No real launcher/controller/wrapper was run. No Torch/project neural module was imported, no actual GPU query was performed, and no NN process was started by this review. Stdlib AST and expression inspection only.
The requested reviewer route is Astra/max, but independent routing attestation is absent. Review independence is same-family, actual_route is UNATTESTED, and acceptance is provisional.

Only the dense_main_pipeline source among the three existing qualified_scope source hashes is present in this bundle. Its hash and the launcher queue hash were independently matched; other remote source/file availability and environment assertions were not tested here.

The supplied five PASS results are executor-recorded mocked host control-flow evidence, not freshly executed reviewer tests or proof of GPU qualification, training, full video evaluation, metrics, or module effectiveness.

The original R2 H/HA training and resource/concurrency decision are context supplied by the parent. This review makes no new claim about their current state and does not create or modify routine observers.
Successful end-to-end execution would still require seven-metric result audit and matched module-effect evidence. Pipeline completion alone is not goal achievement.
